Name: Casey Barrett
Brief description of intervention(s) the: My research works on a host-directed genetic and biological intervention to enhance wheat’s innate defence mechanisms against Zymoseptoria tritici, the causal agent of Septoria tritici blotch disease (STB). STB is a major foliar disease of wheat currently managed primarily through fungicide application and resistance breeding. However the rapidly evolving nature of the pathogen leads to the need for identification of additional host genes in order to support sustainable resistance and reduce reliance on chemical fungicides. This project functionally characterises wheat genes involved in key regulatory pathways associated with stress adaptation. This intervention aligns with clean and healthy planet outcome by targeting host genetic diversity within the wheat biosphere. This enhances plant production under stress, reduces fungicide dependency and supports sustained cereal disease management.
